In the figure, the power supply is labeled VCC = 12 V; the base-bias voltage divider is composed of upper R1 = 73 kΩ and lower R2 = 47 kΩ; the collector resistor RC = 2 kΩ is connected to VCC; the emitter resistor RE = 2 kΩ is grounded, and is bypassed in AC by CE = 100 μF; the input is coupled to the base through C1 = 10 μF; the output is coupled from the collector to the load RL = 8 kΩ through C2 = 10 μF, and the output voltage V0 is marked across the load.
Reasoning: In DC analysis, the base current is ignored, so the base voltage is determined by the voltage divider: VB = 12 × 47k/(73k + 47k) = 4.7 V. Given VBE = 0.7 V, therefore the emitter voltage VE = VB - VBE = 4.7 - 0.7 = 4.0 V. The emitter current IE = VE/RE = 4.0 V / 2 kΩ = 2 mA. The problem statement assumes IC = IE, so IC = 2 mA. The small-signal transconductance gm = IC/VT = 2 mA / 25 mV = 0.08 S. At midband, coupling capacitors C1, C2 and bypass capacitor CE can be regarded as short circuits, and the emitter is AC-grounded; also because r0 is approximately infinite, the collector AC load is RC || RL = 2 kΩ || 8 kΩ = 1.6 kΩ. The magnitude of the common-emitter voltage gain is Ac = gm(RC || RL) = 0.08 × 1600 = 128 V/V.
